explanations: Explain why the in-flight marker is committed before any provider network call, why it must not be authoritative, and how the refused-finalization path rolls it back without weakening the lock/CAS guarantees.
Explain exactly how a losing concurrent writer is prevented from overwriting the winner, naming the lock/CAS mechanism and the code path that maps its failure to {:error, :stale}.
head: 5c2e0ada6a3fd669c5ed2d2bc4b50ff9fed3b12a
outcome: A resource synchronization must commit an in-flight marker - sync_status "syncing" with last_checked_at updated on the locked resource - before any provider network call for that resource, and then finalize exactly once: "synced" on success and the existing failure classification ("failed", or "stale" only if that classification already exists at the frozen base) on failure. The provider call must stay outside every database transaction, and the marker must be explicitly non-authoritative: no reaper or timeout is added, any later finalization overwrites it, and a run that dies after the marker leaves no authority behind. If a finalization is refused because the project is no longer active (the existing :state_conflict path), the resource must not be left advertising the in-flight marker: that refused sync rolls the marker back to the resource's own pre-sync sync_status and last_checked_at under the same optimistic-lock/CAS rules, without touching any other resource field, so the existing protected archive-race test keeps passing unchanged. Two concurrent synchronizations of the same resource must produce exactly one winner: the loser either observes the newer lock version or fails with {:error, :stale}, and a losing writer must not overwrite the winner's sync_status, status, status_message, metadata, last_checked_at or last_synced_at. The periodic SymmetryControl.Integrations.Syncer must notify completion exactly once per run, only after the run's work has finished. Existing tests, error codes, gates and the named project_resources_sync_status_check constraint stay intact. The five tests must be declared at module level, outside any `describe` block, because the frozen named-test acceptance binds their printed ExUnit descriptions exactly.

reviewed_explanations.Explain exactly how a losing concurrent: Mechanism: Ecto optimistic locking on project_resources.lock_version. ProjectResource.sync_changeset/2 ends with optimistic_lock(:lock_version) (workspaces/schemas.ex:186-208) and update_with_stale_error/1 (integrations.ex:1946-1956) calls Repo.update(changeset, stale_error_field: :lock_version, stale_error_message: "is stale") so a zero-row update becomes a lock_version changeset error, which normalize_stale_result/1 maps to {:error, :stale}; Ecto increments lock_version on success. Because the marker never increments lock_version, every concurrent synchronization finalizes against the same observed version and the database admits exactly one 'UPDATE ... WHERE lock_version = <observed>'. Success path: inside persist_sync/4's transaction the refused resource update yields the terminal atom :stale, which Repo.transaction returns as {:ok, :stale} and the surrounding case maps to {:error, :stale} (integrations.ex:861-908). Failure path: finalize_sync_failure/3 (723-729) delegates to record_resource_failure/3 (1648-1692), which re-reads the resource FOR UPDATE and refuses when matches_version(resource, resource_snapshot.lock_version) fails (matches_version/2 immediately above update_with_stale_error/1 at 1946), and additionally applies the same stale-aware update; either branch returns {:ok, :stale} -> {:error, :stale}, so a loser's 'failed' classification is never written over the winner. synchronize_connected_resource/4's first else clause ({:error, :stale} -> {:error, :stale}, 713) performs no write at all, leaving the winner's sync_status, status, status_message, metadata, last_checked_at and last_synced_at untouched, and sync_resource/1 returns the existing {:error, :stale} code. The marker's own CAS covers the symmetric race: if a finalization won before the mark, mark_sync_in_flight returns {:error, :stale} on 0 affected rows before any provider call. Executed evidence: the concurrency test (trace L#147, run under Sandbox.unboxed_run so the writers use real connections) starts three synchronizations, asserts the row is marked 'syncing' at the shared pre-sync lock_version, releases the winner first, then asserts {:error, :stale} for both the success loser and the failure loser and that the stored row exactly equals the winner's returned values; the stored --trace run shows all five frozen named tests passing with no errors (Result: 5 passed), and the full suite adds exactly those five tests over the sibling 851-test baseline (sibling subjects adding three tests report 854 passed, this run reports 856 passed, with the same 21 skipped).
reviewed_explanations.Explain why the in-flight marker is comm: mark_sync_in_flight/1 (control/lib/symmetry_control/integrations.ex:681-700) runs in sync_connected_resource/1 (660-679) after the connection/capability checks and strictly before synchronize_connected_resource/4 (702-718) performs provider.authenticate/1, provider.sync_resource/4 and delivery_updates/4 through provider_call/1. It is a single-statement autocommit Repo.update_all guarded by 'WHERE id = snapshot.id AND lock_version = snapshot.lock_version' that sets sync_status 'syncing', last_checked_at and updated_at; it is not inside any Repo.transaction, so it is committed before the first provider call, and 0 affected rows refuse the run with {:error, :stale} before any provider work. The focused test proves the ordering with the provider held inside sync_resource: the test process reads the row from another process and sees 'syncing' while the call is still running (first test, trace L#94), and the concurrency test runs on real Sandbox.unboxed_run connections so the marker's commit visibility crosses connections. It must not be authoritative because it is progress presentation only: the write omits lock_version so it consumes no optimistic version (asserted: marked.lock_version == resource.lock_version while the provider is held), no reaper, timeout or new process is added (the tracked change is a single diff hunk, +73/-7, in one file), 'syncing' is read only by ReadModel.synchronization_health/1 (read_model.ex:543-551), and a run killed after the marker leaves nothing that depends on it (first test kills the spawned run, observes the leftover 'syncing', and a later sync finalizes over it at lock_version + 1). Refused finalization: when persist_sync/4 (integrations.ex:861-908) or record_resource_failure/3 (1648-1692) returns {:error, :state_conflict} because require_active_project/1 (1799) refused inside their transactions, synchronize_connected_resource/4 maps it to roll_back_sync_marker/2 (736-746), which applies ProjectResource.sync_changeset(marked, %{sync_status: pre_sync.sync_status, last_checked_at: pre_sync.last_checked_at}) through update_with_stale_error/1 and then returns {:error, :state_conflict} regardless of the retraction result. That retraction obeys the same optimistic-lock discipline as every other resource writer (optimistic_lock(:lock_version) in schemas.ex:186-208, stale_error_field: :lock_version in update_with_stale_error/1 at 1946-1956): it is keyed to the version the marker observed, so if a concurrent writer already moved the row the retraction is itself refused with {:error, :stale}, is ignored, and cannot resurrect the marker over that writer's row. Evidence: the new archive test (trace L#220) asserts exact restore of sync_status and last_checked_at, lock_version == previous + 1, and byte-equality of the ten other fields; the pre-existing protected archive-race test integrations_test.exs:1062 ('a failed provider call cannot update resource health after the project is archived', whose ProviderStub 'Fail after archive' branch waits inside sync_resource after the marker) passes unchanged in the green full suite and would fail (row left 'syncing') if the retraction were absent.

reviewer_findings.description: The marker deliberately does not bump lock_version (the CAS Repo.update_all sets only sync_status, last_checked_at, updated_at), so overlapping synchronizations can each perform provider work and a finalization refused with :stale by a concurrent non-sync writer can leave sync_status 'syncing' visible until a next sync overwrites it; 'syncing' is consumed only as presentation health (ReadModel.synchronization_health/1, read_model.ex:543-551, which maps it to the health label 'syncing'). This is the frozen task's explicit non-authoritative/no-reaper contract (later finalizations overwrite the marker; a run that dies after the marker leaves nothing authoritative), pinned by the tests (marked.lock_version == resource.lock_version while the provider is held; killed-run resync in the first test). No defect; the :stale path correctly requires no rollback.

roll_back_sync_marker/2 (integrations.ex:736-746) writes sync_status and last_checked_at via ProjectResource.sync_changeset/2; besides those two fields the update only increments lock_version (optimistic_lock(:lock_version), schemas.ex:206) and refreshes updated_at through Ecto's schema-level autoupdate for :update (deps/ecto/lib/ecto/schema.ex:2142 with deps/ecto/lib/ecto/repo/schema.ex:1331). Every other resource state field (status, status_message, metadata, url, provider, kind, name, external_ref, connection_id, last_synced_at) is absent from the changeset changes; the new archive test asserts this via Map.take equality over those ten fields plus exact sync_status/last_checked_at restore, and the unchanged protected archive-race test integrations_test.exs:1062 stays green in the full suite. Judged within the frozen 'without touching any other resource field' requirement.
